title: Pack and unpack a ZIP archive, awaited
summary: Pack in-memory text files, from a few bytes to several hundred kilobytes, into a deflate-compressed ZIP archive and read every entry back out of it, through each package's awaited API.
notes: The files of deflate-roundtrip, through packages that write and read ZIP only through promises or callbacks, with one operation at a time: each operation packs the entries into a deflated ZIP archive in memory, reads every entry back from those bytes and returns both, awaited before the next operation starts. The archive itself is read by the scenario's own strict ZIP reader. The figure is the package's ZIP work (headers, CRC-32, the central directory, deflate and inflate) plus the promise and event-loop turns it needs; zip.js and @quentinadam/zip compress through the runtime's CompressionStream, whose work a runtime may do off the JavaScript thread, and fflate deflates files of 160,000 bytes or more in a worker thread it starts for each; CPU is that of the whole process, every thread included. In memory only, no file system, no timer or sleep.
